Header: Internal roadmap/launch readiness engineering sync
Date: 2026-08-12 10:00 PDT | Duration: 1:15 | Recorded by: fireflies bot
Attendees: Maria, Daniel, Priya, Lucas, Emily, Aaron, Samir
---
[00:00] Maria: okay everyone thanks for joining, we've got a full agenda, q4 launch readiness, quick incident recap from july 28, and then canary/rollout decisions. we'll try to keep this tight.
[00:15] Daniel: sounds good. i'll start with the infra updates — we've got the autoscaler patch in staging, priya validated the kernel selection changes on the inference nodes, but there's one odd perf regression at longer seqs.
[00:30] Priya: yeah the kernel path looks good for 8k tokens but there's a jitter when the kv cache warms, sometimes the traces show "K V cash" errors in the logs — probably a transcription in the log messages, but i mean kv cache thrash.
[00:45] Lucas: the regression seems tied to continous batching heuristics — when we hit mixed seq lengths the batcher mis-estimates memory and we end up with higher GC pauses. i put a patch that forces a 5ms scheduling window to smooth it.
[01:00] Emily: is that going to affect latency SLO? our target for interactive flows is p95 < 200ms for hosted API.
[01:12] Daniel: with the 5ms window p95 drops to ~185 on our local runs, but throughput cost goes up ~8%. tradeoff.
[01:25] Maria: okay capture that tradeoff; product prefers to keep latency under 200 at launch even if unit cost is +5-10%, but we need a clear path to reduce cost post-launch.
[01:40] Aaron: on the release side, can we commit to a 2-week canary where we ramp by traffic buckets? my plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over two weeks with rollback gates at each step.
[01:56] Priya: network-wise we need the VPC peering and route updates applied to staging. note: some of the docs still say VP C peering which confuses people. i'll update.
[02:10] Samir: quick note on the july 28 outage — root cause was the autoscaler hitting a race when scaling down GPUs; we saw a capacity hole for ~22 minutes which caused tail latency spikes and some 5xxs.
[02:25] Lucas: i wrote up a timeline, adding it to the postmortem notes link. the fix is in staging but we need a canary to verify it holds at scale. also we need an SLO impact calc for the execs.
[02:40] Emily: i'd like to see the SLO calc before we commit to the launch date. can we get a slide for the exec sync tomorrow?
[02:48] Maria: yes, emily and daniel can pair on that. emily will own product acceptance criteria and daniel will own perf numbers.
[02:58] Daniel: noted. for benchmarks, i'm proposing two scenarios: typical interactive chat (2-3 turns, median seq 256) and long-context retrieval (8k tokens). the sheet has both.
[03:15] Maria: good. anything on security/compliance? we need SOC 2 and the audit logs for private deployments.
[03:23] Priya: security docs are mostly ready. KMS integrations for customer-managed keys are in the checklist but i need to confirm HSM signing with compliance. i'll ping legal.
[03:35] Aaron: for private/on-prem we need a separate runbook for upgrade windows because some customers will schedule maintenance during specific business hours.
[03:45] Samir: also the incident runbook — it didn't fully capture the autoscaler scale-down flapping. i propose adding a pre-scale verification step.
[03:55] Lucas: agreed, and add a tracing hook to correlate kernel selection with batch composition — that was missing.
[04:05] Maria: next, rollout policy: do we want auto-fallback to previous model variant if quality metrics degrade during canary?
[04:12] Daniel: yes, and tie fallback to a specific metric set: perplexity + rerank score threshold; we'll have the eval harness emit a pass/fail signal. note: some of the telemetry labels got swapped in the harness, i've got a ticket to fix that.
[04:30] Priya: infra ask: i need 12 more GPU slots in dedicated pool for the stress tests — the ops budget has wiggle room if we can justify it.
[04:40] Maria: approve provisional 12 slots for one week for benchmark runs. daniel, runbook the exact hours so billing is predictable.
[04:50] Daniel: will do.
[04:55] Emily: on product acceptance, two big items: feature parity with beta (tool-calling and structured output) and no regressions on hallucination metrics for our key prompts.
[05:10] Maria: set the hallucination regression threshold at <2% above baseline for launch. if we exceed that, we delay or rollback.
[05:20] Aaron: deployment timeline proposal — freeze on 2026-08-24, canary start 2026-08-25, full rollout 2026-09-08 assuming gates pass.
[05:32] Samir: can we compress the freeze window if the load test is clean?
[05:38] Maria: yes but let's plan conservatively. we need the exec signoff before moving earlier.
[05:45] Lucas: incident follow-up: i've got a quick patch to the autoscaler that changes the cooldown heuristic from 30s to 90s. it reduces flapping in staging. downside: slower scale-down, small cost increase.
[05:58] Daniel: recommend making cooldown configurable per pool so dedicated pools can be aggressive and hosted pools conservative.
[06:06] Priya: also we discovered that quantized kernels for some models cause small accuracy deltas on longer context — need to pin quantization profile per model at rollout.
[06:20] Emily: product wants a list of pinned model profiles per workload by 2026-08-14.
[06:28] Maria: lucas and daniel to produce that.
[06:35] Aaron: small ops note: support playbooks need clear instructions for escalations OOO and on-call rotations during canary. i'll update rota.
[06:44] Samir: i'll test the alerting thresholds in staging; current thresholds were tuned pre-quantization and may not trigger correctly.
[06:52] Maria: action items recap — daniel load test, priya networking & runbook updates, lucas postmortem and autoscaler changes, aaron canary schedule, emily acceptance criteria. anything else?
[07:05] Emily: we should loop in legal on the KMS/HSM note — they might want extra paperwork.
[07:12] Priya: noted, will ping legal.
[07:18] Maria: ok last bit: exec slide for tomorrow — emily and daniel to produce a one-pager: launch readiness status (green/yellow/red), key risks, and canary plan. share by EOD 2026-08-13.
[07:30] Daniel: copy.
[07:36] Maria: thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.
